questions.q: A long straight wire of a circular cross-section with radius ' $a$ ' carries a steady current $I$. The current I is uniformly distributed across this cross-section. The plot of magnitude of magnetic field B with distance $r$ from the centre of the wire is given by

questions.solution: We know inside the wire $\begin{array}{ll} B=\frac{\mu_0 I}{2 \pi R^2} \cdot r & (O \lt r \lt R) \\ \text { And } B=\frac{\mu_0 I}{2 \pi r} & \text { for }(R \lt r) \end{array}$

The velocities at P and Q are respectively, vi→ and -2vj→ . Then which of the following statements (A, B, C, D) are the correct? (Trajectory shown is schematic and not to scale)



A E=32mv2qa

C Rate of work done by both the fields at Q is zero
D The difference between the magnitude of angular momentum of the particle at P and Q is 2mav .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
(A) by work energy theorem

Wmag+Wele=12m(2v)2-12m(v)2

0+qE02a=32mv2
E0=34mv2qa

(B) Rate of work done at A= power of electric force

=qE0V
=34mv3a

(C) at Q,dwdt=0 for both forces

D ΔL→=(-m2 v 2ak^)-(- mvak )

|ΔL→|=3mva

questions.solution:
Force per unit length between two parallel wires is Fl=μ0i1i22πd

Then, 2×10-6=4π2×10-7i22π×0.2

questions.q:
A proton moving with a constant velocity passes through a region of space without any change in its velocity. If E→ and B→ represent the electric and magnetic fields respectively, then the region of space may have :
(A) E=0, B=0; (B) E=0, B≠0; (C) E≠0, B=0; (D) E≠0, B≠0

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Net force on proton inside an electric and a magnetic field is given by

F→e+F→m=qE→+qv→×B→    ...1

If both E→ and B→ are zero, then F→e and F→m both are zero. Hence, velocity may remain constant. Therefore, option (A) is correct.

If E=0, B≠0, but velocity is parallel or antiparallel to the magnetic field, then also F→e and F→m both are zero. Hence, option (B) is also correct.

If E≠0, B≠0, but F→e + F→m=0, then also velocity may remain constant. Thus, option (D) is also correct.

thus v1:v2:v3=1 mp:12mp:14mp=11:12:14=4:2:1.

questions.q: A metal surface is illuminated by a radiation of wavelength <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4500</mn><mover><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow><mo>∘</mo></mover></math>. The ejected photo-electron enters a constant magnetic field of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mT</mi></math> making an angle of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>90</mn><mo>°</mo></math> with the magnetic field. If it starts revolving in a circular path of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math>, the work function of the metal is approximately
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
From the Einstein's photoelectric equation K=hcλ-ϕ⇒ϕ=hcλ-K

Now R=mvBq⇒v=RBqm⇒K=R2B2q22m

Therefore, ϕ=hcλ-R2B2q22m=6.63×10-34×3×1084500×10-10-2×10-3×2×10-3×1.6×10-1922×9.1×10-31⇒ϕ=4.42-2.25×10-19 J=2.271.6 eV=1.36 eV

questions.q: The magnetic moment of an electron <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mi>e</mi></mfenced></math> revolving in an orbit around nucleus with an orbital angular momentum is given by
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{M}}=\mathrm{IA}$
$\Rightarrow|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{M}}|=\frac{\mathrm{e}}{\frac{2 \pi \mathrm{R}}{\mathrm{v}}} \pi \mathrm{R}^2\left[\because \mathrm{I}=\frac{\mathrm{Q}}{\mathrm{T}}=\frac{\mathrm{e}}{\frac{2 \pi \mathrm{R}}{\mathrm{V}}}\right]$
$\Rightarrow|\vec{M}|=\frac{1}{2} e v R \Rightarrow|\vec{M}|=\frac{\mathrm{mvR}}{1} \cdot \frac{\mathrm{e}}{2 \mathrm{~m}}$
$\Rightarrow|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{M}}|=\frac{\mathrm{eL}}{2 \mathrm{~m}} \Rightarrow|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{M}}|=-\frac{\mathrm{e} \overrightarrow{\mathrm{L}}}{2 \mathrm{~m}}$
[ $\because$ Here $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{M}}$ and $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{L}}$ will always be opposite]

questions.q: For a moving coil galvanometer, the deflection in the coil is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>05</mn><mo> </mo><mi>rad</mi></math> when a current of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mA</mi></math> is passed through it. If the torsional constant of suspension wire is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo> </mo><mo>×</mo><mo> </mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>–</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi>rad</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>, the magnetic field is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>01</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></math> and the number of turns in the coil is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>200</mn></math>, the area of each turn (in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>cm</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math> ) is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given: θ=0.05 rad, I=10 mA, K=4×10-5 N m rad-1, B=0.01 T, N=200

The torsional constant of a wire used in a moving coil galvanometer is given by 

K=NIABθ, where, A is area of each turn

So, A=KθNIB=4×10-5×0.05200×10×10-3×0.01

Thus, A=10-4 m2=1 cm2

questions.q:
An infinitely long hollow conducting cylinder with radius R carries a uniform current along its surface.

Choose the correct representation of magnetic field Bas a function of radial distance r from the axis of cylinder.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
According to Ampere's law,

∮B→·dl→=μ0i

Inside the hollow cylinder, current will be zero. Therefore, magnetic field will also be zero.

Outside the cylinder,

B2πr=μ0i⇒B=μ0i2πr⇒B∝1r

Hence, the correct answer is D.

questions.q: A circular coil having 200 turns, $2.5 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~m}^2$ area and carrying $100 \mu \mathrm{A}$ current is placed in a uniform magnetic field of 1T. Initially the magnetic dipole moment $(\vec{M})$ was directed along $\vec{B}$. Amount of work, required to rotate the coil through $90^{\circ}$ from its initial orientation such that $\vec{M}$ becomes perpendicular to $\vec{B}$, is ______ $\mu \mathrm{J}$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: We know $\begin{aligned} \mathrm{W}_{\text {ext }} & =\Delta \mathrm{U}+\Delta \mathrm{KE} \quad(\text { P.E. }=-\overrightarrow{\mathrm{M}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathrm{B}}) \\ & =-\overrightarrow{\mathrm{M}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathrm{B}}_{\mathrm{f}}+\overrightarrow{\mathrm{M}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathrm{B}}_{\mathrm{i}}+0 \\ & =-\mathrm{MB} \cos 90+\mathrm{MB} \cos 0 \\ & =\mathrm{MB} \\ & =\mathrm{NIAB} \\ & =200 \times 100 \times 10^{-6} \times \frac{5}{2} \times 10^{-4} \times 1=5 \mu \mathrm{J} \end{aligned}$
